is not shining, but rather dark and bruised with a deathly earthiness. Similarly, <term>Moon</term> <gloss>silver</gloss> is also turned yellow by the solution of <term>Mars</term> <gloss>iron</gloss>.

The method of <term>citrination</term> <gloss>turning yellow or gold-colored</gloss> which is accomplished through <term>Vitriol</term> <gloss>sulfate minerals</gloss> or <term>copperas</term> is as follows. Let a certain quantity of each of these be taken, and let that part which allows itself to be <term>sublimed</term> <gloss>vaporized and resolidified</gloss> be lifted up, until it is totally <term>sublimed</term> with outward pressure. After this, let that which was <term>sublimed</term> be <term>sublimed</term> again with the method of fire appropriate to it, so that one part after another may be <term>fixed</term> <gloss>made resistant to heat</gloss> from it, until the greater part of it is <term>fixed</term>. Afterward, let it be administered with the intention of a cautious fire, so that a greater fire can be applied to it for its perfection. After this, let it be dissolved into a most red water, to which there is no equal. From there, you must devise a way to provide its entry into the <term>Lunar body</term> <gloss>silver</gloss>. These methods have been sufficiently shown to you already, if you have been a diligent seeker of the perfect work which we have written.

And because we see these things adhere amicably to the depths of <term>Moon</term> <gloss>silver</gloss>, we have therefore considered it, and it is certain, that these are from their same root, and therefore it happens that they are altered by them. These indeed are all the medicines of the <term>first order</term> <note>the basic level of alchemical medicines which cause superficial changes</note> that we have brought forward. However, many more of their methods can be multiplied, provided the essence of the <term>pigmental</term> <gloss>coloring</gloss> things remains the same throughout the variety of methods. Some people have indeed devised more medicines, but one of two things must necessarily happen: either it is necessary to create the medicine from the same substances, or from those having the same nature. Or they compose a medicine which is equivalent to that which does not exist, along with its own alteration; one which contributes nothing to the world, nor to the parts of the world, until the mover in the high mobile nature has come to rest uncorrupted.

<summary>This page details the process of citrination using iron and vitriol to color silver. It explains the necessity of repeated sublimation and fixation to create a red solvent for metallic transformation.</summary>
<keywords>citrination, silver, iron, vitriol, copperas, sublimation, fixation, first order medicines, alchemy</keywords>
